newsitem.title: JAPAN: BRIDGESTONE TARGETS S-E ASIA FOR TYRES GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: BRIDGESTONE TARGETS S-E ASIA FOR TYRES GROWTH.

text.p: Japan's Bridgestone Corp is boosting its offshore tyre output, especially in Southeast Asia, in a bid to achieve its goal of grabbing 20 percent of the global tyre market.
The company also may expand into potentially high-growth markets like China, Russia and eastern Europe, Bridgestone's manager of public relations, Kenichi Kitawaki, said in an interview.
Bridgestone will invest about 26 billion yen ($234 million) in an Indonesian joint venture to build a plant, which it hopes will produce 40 tonnes of tyres per day beginning in 1997.
It also plans to boost tyre output at an existing facility in Thailand to 80 tonnes per day from the current 36 tonnes by late 1998.

"In order to meet our target of acquiring a 20 percent share of the world tyre market, we need to increase tyre output in overseas markets because tyre output at home has nearly hit a ceiling," Kitawaki said.
Bridgestone captured 19 percent of the total global market in 1995 in dollar terms, up from 17.9 percent in 1994, according to the U.S. trade magazine Tire Business.

"In the Southeast Asia market, double-digit growth in demand for tyres will continue in the next few years," Kitawaki said. "Not only our company, but also other tyre makers are keenly investing in the region.
The company currently has about 40 percent of the tyre market in Indonesia and 56 percent in Thailand, but Kitawaki added: "Unless we raise output, we will lose market share in the region."
Kitawaki said Bridgestone's investment plans for Russia and eastern Europe are still on the drawing board.
In the near term it hopes to boost exports to those regions but will eventually need to build factories there if it is to maintain its global market share, Kitawaki said.

He said the mature markets of the United States and western Europe, where Bridgestone already has production facilities and holds a market share of 16 percent and 13 percent respectively, offered few opportunities for growth.

In Japan, where Bridgestone accounts for nearly 50 percent of total tyre production, the company plans to lift output to a record 540,000 tonnes of tyres in 1996, up modestly from last year's 520,000 tonnes.
Of that, 250,000 to 260,000 tonnes will be exported, mostly to the Middle East, Asia and Africa.
The rise in output reflects robust demand for snow tyres in Japan during last winter's unusually heavy snowfall, while the yen's weakness against the dollar also spurred exports.

He added that, in order to maintain output levels in Japan even as production is shifted overseas, domestic plants would increasingly specialise in high-technology products, such as tyres for large trucks and sports cars. ($1=111 yen)
